findings.title: Keep the old index until the replacement is committed
findings.body: An interrupted write leaves the next startup with neither index. Keep the old file until the replacement has been written and committed.
findings.summary: An interrupted replacement can leave the next startup without either index.

findings.title: Reuse the existing temporary-directory fixture
findings.body: The shared fixture already removes its temporary directory after a failed assertion. Reusing it would remove the duplicate cleanup path.
findings.summary: The shared fixture would remove duplicate cleanup code.

findings.title: Keep file ownership in the index writer
findings.body: Moving the replacement operation into the writer would give one component responsibility for creating and committing the new file.
findings.summary: The writer should own both creation and commit of the replacement.

concept_summary: Replacing the index in one operation reduces the recovery states that callers must handle. The writer still needs a clear rule for when the replacement becomes durable.

alternatives.name: Commit through a temporary file
alternatives.concept: Write the replacement beside the existing index and rename it after commit.
alternatives.benefit: A failed write leaves the current index available.
alternatives.cost: The update temporarily needs space for both copies.
alternatives.unresolved: Directory synchronization still needs to be checked on each supported platform.

review_memory.title: A failed cleanup can leave a stale temporary file
review_memory.body: A subsequent update can reuse the stale temporary filename. Remove or replace it before writing a new index.
review_memory.reason: The cleanup path is unchanged in this revision.
review_memory.summary: A later update can reuse a temporary file left by failed cleanup.

review_memory.title: Release the file lock after a failed write
review_memory.summary: A failed update could prevent the next update from acquiring the lock.
review_memory.body: The error path returned before releasing the file lock. The new scope guard now releases the lock on every exit.
review_memory.reason: The scope guard covers the early return.

limitations: The storage failure scenario was checked in source; it was not reproduced on a running node.
